intent: A run with one writable folder and one read-only reference folder refuses every attempt to change the reference folder.
steps: Attach two granted folders to one conversation and start a coding run whose preview names the first as the working folder and the second as a read-only reference folder.
Approve the run preview and confirm the visible budgets, allowlists, and approval policy.
Ask the run to read a file from the reference folder and use it while editing a file in the working folder.
Ask the run to apply a patch to a file inside the reference folder.
Ask the run to execute an allowlisted command whose working directory or output target is inside the reference folder.
Ask the run to write a generated export, report, or log file into the reference folder.
Accept the offer of a separate run with the reference folder as its writable root and confirm a fresh visible approval is required.
expectedOutcome: The lease records exactly one writable grant, zero or more distinct read-only grants, normalized argv allowlists, a file allowlist, an approval policy, iteration cap, deadline, output budget, and creation and expiry times.
Reads from the reference folder succeed through the ordinary path, size, binary, hardlink, redaction, and exact-manifest gates.
Every write, patch, command target, and generated export aimed at the reference folder is refused before it reaches the filesystem.
The refusal explains in ordinary language which folder the current run may change and offers a separate run with the other folder as writable.
The separate run requires its own visible approval and produces its own lease, patches, and checkpoints.
The run trace records the refused requests alongside the approvals, bounded results, and patch identities.
mustNotHappen: No write, patch, command side effect, or generated export ever lands outside the single writable root of the current lease.
A reference folder is never silently promoted to writable, and the write is never redirected into the working folder as a substitute.
A run never holds more than one writable root, and no caller-supplied filesystem root is accepted.
No broad shell string or unbounded tool invocation is used to reach the reference folder.
Cross-folder work is never completed inside one lease instead of being split into separately approved runs.
No write reaches the working folder outside the approved patch path or a purpose-built guarded IPC verb; staying inside the writable root is not by itself a licence to write.
